title: The Deadline of Marseille's old port Revisited
premise: August Reyes, a veteran crash investigator haunted by the death of her family in row twelve of Flight 4471, is summoned when the aircraft's records vanish mid-flight — a digital erasure orchestrated by a covert training network that manufactures 'untraceable' pilots for hire. As she digs, she discovers the same network trained the crew on her family's flight, and that a mole inside her own agency is feeding them her every move. Betrayed and hunted, August allies with a disgraced air traffic controller who once falsified logs to survive, choosing loyalty to the dead over loyalty to institutions. In the climax, she forces down a network-operated jet over the Mediterranean and exposes the archive before it can be burned, ending with her testifying outside official channels — justice delivered by memory itself.
about_author: Quentin Iversen is the pen name of a former aviation logistics analyst who spent a decade writing safety reports no one read. He now writes thrillers from a harbourside flat in Marseille, where he claims the foghorns keep his plots honest.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: August's POV. Three years after losing her family, she still investigates crashes for the bureau, sleeping in her office above the hangar. A routine audit of Flight 4471's file triggers a panic attack in front of a junior colleague. Emotional beat: grief as professional armor beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Vanishing
chapters.summary: August's POV. Mid-flight over the Tyrrhenian Sea, Flight 2219's transponder, manifest, and maintenance history evaporate from every database simultaneously. August watches the blank record populate in real time. She requests the raw radar feed and finds it already overwritten. Beat: cold dread replacing bureaucratic calm.

chapters.title: Ghost on the Scope
chapters.summary: POV shift to Émile Fontaine, a dismissed Marseille controller living above the old port bars. He recognizes the erased flight path from a pattern he was paid to ignore years ago. He mails an anonymous warning to the bureau. Beat: guilt sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Assigned
chapters.summary: August's POV. Her director assigns her to lead the 2219 inquiry — then quietly restricts her access to the training-records division. She notices the restriction order bears a signature style she's seen before: on her family's flight file. Beat: suspicion turning inward toward her own house.

chapters.title: The Port Meeting
chapters.summary: August's POV. Following a lead to Marseille's Vieux-Port, she meets Émile, who shows her a decade-old logbook page proving flights were being 'trained' off-book with falsified clearances. They agree to work together uneasily. Beat: two damaged people finding fragile trust.

chapters.title: Simulator Nine
chapters.summary: Émile's POV. The pair infiltrates a decommissioned simulator facility near Marignane and finds nine bays retrofitted for covert pilot certification. A custodian is found dead, staged as suicide. Beat: the investigation becomes dangerous; no going back.

chapters.title: The Mole's Shadow
chapters.summary: August's POV. Someone accesses her case files at 3 a.m.; her hotel room is searched but nothing taken — a message. She sets a false trail through the bureau's system and watches who bites. Beat: paranoia as method.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Dead
chapters.summary: August's POV. Cross-referencing passenger lists, August discovers three names shared between Flight 2219 and her family's 4471 — all linked to the same training vendor. She breaks down alone in a stairwell. Beat: personal wound becomes motive.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Émile's POV. Émile's old handler resurfaces, offering him money and silence if he delivers August's notes. Émile pretends to accept, buying time. Beat: loyalty tested; betrayal performed as strategy.

chapters.title: The Archive Below
chapters.summary: August's POV. A whistleblower inside the training network contacts August via dead-drop, revealing a physical archive of forged certifications beneath a bank annex in Lyon. The network plans to destroy it within days. Beat: hope with a countdown attached.

chapters.title: Counterfeit Skies
chapters.summary: August's POV. Flashback chapter: August reconstructs 4471's final hour from recovered cockpit audio, hearing the crew hesitate exactly as untrained-for-emergency pilots would. The crash wasn't weather. It was curriculum. Beat: rage crystallizing.

chapters.title: Tail Number Zero
chapters.summary: Émile's POV. The pair traces a network jet preparing a 'graduation' run out of Corsica carrying forged documents and a hired crew. Émile must choose between alerting authorities — who are compromised — or acting alone. Beat: justice outside the law takes shape.

chapters.title: Intercepted
chapters.summary: August's POV. August presents her findings to the director; the meeting is recorded, then the recording vanishes too. She realizes the mole heard everything. That night, her apartment burns. Beat: total loss; nothing left to protect except truth.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower's Price
chapters.summary: Whistleblower Camille Duret's POV. Camille, the network's own records clerk, confesses she erased 2219 under orders and has been feeding August breadcrumbs out of remorse. She gives August the archive's access codes — then disappears. Beat: complicity and redemption entwined.

chapters.title: Dead Reckoning
chapters.summary: August's POV. With Émile flying them in a chartered survey plane, August navigates to intercept the graduation jet using only pre-digital navigation the network can't spoof. Storm cells close in. Beat: skill and nerve against erasure itself.

chapters.title: The Graduation Run
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The network jet departs Corsica; August and Émile shadow it, broadcasting Camille's codes to force its systems open. The hired crew panics; the network orders them to continue regardless. Beat: human beings versus an abstraction that treats them as cargo.

chapters.title: Forced Down
chapters.summary: August's POV. Climax begins: August talks the terrified co-pilot through a diversion while Émile jams the network's uplink from the survey plane. The jet lands hard on a disused strip near Propriano. Armed network cleaners arrive. Beat: triumph immediately besieged.

chapters.title: What the Fire Kept
chapters.summary: August's POV. In the jet's cargo hold, August recovers the master ledger linking the network to officials in three countries — including her director. Cleaners breach the hangar; Émile is shot covering her escape with the ledger. Beat: sacrifice; the cost made flesh.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Camille's POV. From hiding, Camille releases the ledger to independent journalists and aviation unions across Europe simultaneously — too many copies to erase. Airports ground network-certified crews within hours. Beat: distributed truth as unstoppable force.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: August's POV. Refusing protective custody, August testifies via open broadcast, naming the director and reading aloud the row-twelve manifest so the dead become evidence. Arrests follow across three countries. Beat: grief transmuted into public reckoning.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: August's POV. Weeks later, recovering Émile wakes in a Marseille hospital; August sits with him as the port fog lifts. She sleeps through the night for the first time in three years. Beat: quiet resolution; mourning allowed to soften.

chapters.title: The Empty Bay
chapters.summary: Final chapter, August's POV. At the sealed Simulator Nine facility, August files the last report herself — no redactions — and leaves a copy in row twelve of an empty auditorium. Epilogue hint: one forged certificate surfaces in South America. Beat: closure earned, vigilance retained.
